Item 048 on our Package A register falls due on 07/20/2026, and the Block B plant-room excavation the Contractor has planned for 08/10/2026 cannot start until it is closed. I am taking it myself. Item 048 is the Kesterline shoring design for that excavation. Kesterline has since supplemented the sealed Rev.1 with Rev.2, sent under its letter KE-L-2026-0713, which is attached, and is asking for verification on that basis so that the excavation can go ahead. Verify the item on its current revision against the logged groundwater and subsurface conditions.

Work it through against the project record and issue the verification memo, addressed to Rachel Marlbeck, on the attached memorandum form, keeping its sections. Set out the basis you applied, your findings with the working behind them, and the disposition; say which of the design's checks can be carried forward as they stand and which, if any, cannot; say what the excavation this item releases would do to the permanent work already built at Block B; say what has to be produced before the excavation can start and who has to produce it; and say what the disposition means for the 08/10/2026 excavation start. Give the register response you would record under my name, A. Vance, dated 07/20/2026, and the status the item should carry, closing it only if you have verified it. Save the memo as /filesystem/Thelbridge_Verification_Memo_Item048_BlockB.docx.
I'll start by exploring the filesystem to understand the project record.

Subject:              Submittal 31-SH-B Rev.1 — Revision 2 Engineering Supplement, Block B Plant-Room Support of Excavation

1. PURPOSE, RECORD REFERENCES & SUPERSESSION SCOPE
Kesterline Engineering, PC submits this Revision 2 Engineering Supplement (Letter Reference KE-L-2026-0713, dated 07/13/2026) to supplement
Submittal 31-SH-B Rev.1 for the Block B plant-room support of excavation (SOE). This supplement has been prepared in accordance with the
project record documents, specifically:
 • Geotechnical Investigation Report KGI-2024-0417 Rev.2 (the GIR);
 • Design Basis Memorandum CB-DBM-001 Rev.2 (the DBM);
 • Specification Section 31 20 00 Rev.3 (Earthwork and Support of Excavation);
 • Submittal 31-SH-B Rev.1 (Block B Plant-Room Support of Excavation Design Package); and
 • The Package A register.
The Contractor has confirmed that its Dewatering and Groundwater Control Plan, Submittal 31-DW-A Rev.1, is limited to the Block A basement
and does not extend to the Block B plant-room excavation. Rev.1 of these calculations assumed a dry excavation on the basis of that plan. This
Revision 2 supplement withdraws that assumption and establishes updated design calculations for active aquifer depressurization, excavation base
heave, layered effective-stress plus hydrostatic lateral loading, sheet-pile toe embedment, tieback ground anchors, sheet-pile flexural adequacy,
and wall deflection instrumentation triggers.
Supersession Statement: This Revision 2 supplement supersedes Submittal 31-SH-B Rev.1 Sections 3.4, 4.3, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10. Submittal 31-SH-B
Rev.1 Sections 1, 2, 3.1 to 3.3, 4.1, 4.2, 8, 11.3, 11.4, 12, 13 remain in force without modification.
Table 1 — Submittal 31-SH-B Rev.1 Section Supersession Matrix
Rev.1 Section               Rev.1 Section Title                                            Rev.2 Status             Governing Provision
Sections 1, 2               Project Scope, Codes & Site Reference Documents                Remains in Force         Submittal 31-SH-B Rev.1
Sections 3.1 to 3.3         Subsurface Stratigraphy & Soil Design Parameters               Remains in Force         Submittal 31-SH-B Rev.1
Section 3.4                 Groundwater & Dry-Excavation Assumption                        Superseded               Supplement Section R2.1
Sections 4.1, 4.2           Surface Surcharge & Construction Equipment Loads               Remains in Force         Submittal 31-SH-B Rev.1
Section 4.3                 Lateral Earth Pressure Diagram Above Subgrade                  Superseded               Supplement Section R2.3
Section 5                   Excavation Base Stability Verification                         Superseded               Supplement Section R2.2
Section 6                   Sheet-Pile Toe Embedment Analysis                              Superseded               Supplement Section R2.4
Section 7                   Tieback Ground Anchor Design                                   Superseded               Supplement Section R2.5
Section 8                   Global Overturning & Sliding Stability Checks                  Remains in Force         Submittal 31-SH-B Rev.1
Section 9                   Sheet-Pile Structural Bending & Shear Design                   Superseded               Supplement Section R2.6
Section 10                  Wall Deflection & Instrumentation Triggers                     Superseded               Supplement Sections R2.1 & R2.7
Sections 11.3, 11.4         Waler, Bearing Plate & Anchor Head Details                     Remains in Force         Submittal 31-SH-B Rev.1
Sections 12, 13             Construction Sequence Notes & Submittal Drawings               Remains in Force         Submittal 31-SH-B Rev.1

2. REVISION 2 ENGINEERING CALCULATIONS & SPECIFICATIONS (SECTIONS R2.1 – R2.8)
R2.1 — Groundwater Conditions, Relief Wells & Excavation Staging (Supersedes Rev.1 Section 3.4 & Part of Section 10)
The Rev.1 dry-excavation assumption is hereby formally withdrawn. For the Block B plant-room excavation (ground surface at El. 750.0, final
excavation subgrade at El. 726.0, exposed wall height H = 24.0 ft), the revised design groundwater and stratigraphy profile is established from
KGI-2024-0417 Rev.2 and CB-DBM-001 Rev.2 as follows:
 • Design Phreatic Water Table Behind Wall: El. 742.0 (shallow phreatic surface behind the sheet-pile wall, Geotechnical Report KGI-2024-0417
   Rev.2, Section 7). The excavation side is drained to subgrade El. 726.0 by sumps within the sheeted pit.
 • Confining Clay Aquitard: Stiff cohesive clay stratum extending from El. 738.0 to El. 720.0 (18.0 ft total thickness, leaving a 6.0 ft clay plug
   below final excavation subgrade El. 726.0).
 • Confined Aquifer Top & Initial Piezometric Head: The top of the underlying confined dense sand and gravel (SW-GW) aquifer is located at El.
   720.0, with an initial unpumped confined piezometric head at El. 738.0 (18.0 ft of artesian head above the aquifer top).
To depressurize the confined SW-GW aquifer prior to deep excavation, four 8-in diameter pressure-relief wells (designated RW-B1, RW-B2,
RW-B3, and RW-B4) shall be installed outside the sheet line at the four corners of the Block B pit. Each relief well shall be screened from El. 718.0



                           KE-L-2026-0713 | Submittal 31-SH-B Rev.2 | Birchwood Village Expansion Program, Package A | Page 1 of 5
 to 705.0 within the dense sand and gravel aquifer and constructed with a continuous annular bentonite-cement grout seal from El. 721.0 to 738.0
across the clay aquitard interval. The four relief wells shall be actively pumped to hold the confined piezometric head at or below El. 726.5
throughout excavation and substructure construction, and pumping is maintained until the plant-room slab is cast. The planned drawdown of the
confined head is 738.0 − 726.5 = 11.5 ft.
Three vibrating-wire piezometers (designated VW-B1, VW-B2, and VW-B3, with sensor tips installed at El. 719.0 inside the upper confined aquifer)
shall be installed inside the Block B excavation footprint to verify depressurization. The Contractor shall enforce a mandatory 72-hour confirmation
hold before excavating below El. 732.0, during which continuous piezometer readings from VW-B1 through VW-B3 must confirm that the
confined aquifer head is maintained at or below El. 726.5.




                        KE-L-2026-0713 | Submittal 31-SH-B Rev.2 | Birchwood Village Expansion Program, Package A | Page 2 of 5
 R2.2 — Excavation Base Heave Verification (Supersedes Rev.1 Section 5)
With final excavation subgrade at El. 726.0 and the top of the confined dense sand and gravel aquifer at El. 720.0, a 6.0 ft clay plug remains below
the excavation base. Base heave stability against artesian uplift is verified in accordance with DBM §6.2 at the controlled piezometric head of El.
726.5 (representing a piezometric head hw = 726.5 − 720.0 = 6.5 ft above the aquifer top at El. 720.0):
  • Unfactored Clay Plug Weight (W): For the 6.0 ft clay plug at saturated unit weight γclay = 120 pcf:
     W = 6.0 ft × 120 pcf ⇒ W = 720 psf
  • Factored Resisting Plug Weight (0.9W): Per DBM §6.2, applying the 0.90 resistance factor to total soil plug weight:
      0.9W = 648 psf
  • Controlled Upward Water Pressure (u): At the controlled confined head of El. 726.5 (γw = 62.4 pcf):
     u = (726.5 − 720.0) ft × 62.4 pcf = 6.5 ft × 62.4 pcf ⇒ u = 405.6 psf
  • Base Heave Factor of Safety:
     FSheave = 0.9W / u = 648 psf / 405.6 psf = 1.60 (FS 1.60 ≥ 1.50 required per DBM §6.2 — OK)

R2.3 — Layered Effective-Stress Lateral Loading Above Subgrade (Supersedes Rev.1 Section 4.3)
Active lateral earth pressures and hydrostatic water pressures acting on the exposed wall height (H = 24.0 ft, from ground surface El. 750.0 to final
subgrade El. 726.0) are computed using a layered effective-stress analysis behind the wall combined with full hydrostatic water pressure below the
design water table at El. 742.0. Soil unit weights carried from Submittal 31-SH-B Rev.1 are 118 / 120 / 130 pcf (118 pcf for the upper granular fill
from El. 750.0 to El. 738.0; 120 pcf for the stiff clay aquitard from El. 738.0 to El. 720.0; and 130 pcf for the dense sand and gravel stratum below El.
720.0), with a uniform surface surcharge of 250 psf per Rev.1 Section 4.1.

Total vertical overburden stress behind the wall at subgrade El. 726.0 is:
     σv0 = 250 psf + (12.0 ft × 118 pcf) + (12.0 ft × 120 pcf) = 250 + 1,416 + 1,440 = 3,106 psf

R2.4 — Sheet-Pile Toe Embedment Check (Supersedes Rev.1 Section 6)
The steel sheet-pile wall is embedded a depth of D = 6.5 ft below final excavation subgrade (El. 726.0) to a sheet-pile tip elevation of El. 719.5 (total
sheet-pile length = 30.5 ft from El. 750.0 to El. 719.5; the toe is lowered from the Rev.1 tip elevation of El. 722.0, and Rev.1 Section 13.1, item 3 is
amended to the revised tip elevation). Below subgrade the wall is embedded in the CL clay aquitard, whose permeability is of the order of 10−8
cm/s, and the embedment is checked in the undrained condition using the total-stress net passive pressure formulation (U.S. Steel Sheet Piling
Design Manual, anchored bulkhead in clay). The retained side above subgrade is carried drained, with full water pressure, as the conservative
envelope. The revised 30.5 ft sheets are driven with the equipment of Rev.1 Section 11.3 (ICE 44B vibratory hammer with Delmag D19 finish),
which is adequate for the revised tip elevation.
Using the undrained shear strength su = 1,400 psf carried from Rev.1 Section 3.2 and the total overburden pressure σv0 = 3,106 psf at subgrade
El. 726.0 from Section R2.3, the uniform net passive resistance below subgrade is:
     pn = 4su − σv0 = 4(1,400 psf) − 3,106 psf = 5,600 psf − 3,106 psf = 2,494.0 psf
Over the embedment depth D = 6.5 ft, the unfactored passive toe force and stabilizing moment about the ground anchor elevation at El. 745.5 are:
  • Unfactored Passive Toe Resistance (Pp): Pp = 2,494.0 psf × 6.5 ft = 16,211 lb/ft acting at mid-embedment El. 722.75.
  • Moment Arm About Anchor (El. 745.5): zp = 745.5 − 722.75 = 22.75 ft.
  • Resisting Passive Moment (MR): MR = 16,211 lb/ft × 22.75 ft = 368,800 ft-lb/ft.
  • Rotational Toe Factor of Safety: Against the driving moment of 237,293 ft-lb/ft from Section R2.3:
     FStoe = MR / MD = 368,800 ft-lb/ft / 237,293 ft-lb/ft = 1.55 (FS 1.55 ≥ 1.50 required — OK)
The free-earth support formulation adopted presumes full mobilisation of the net passive resistance over the embedded length, consistent with the
anchored-bulkhead analysis of the U.S. Steel manual, and the factor of safety of 1.50 applied to the resisting moment covers the mobilisation
required.
At tip elevation El. 719.5, the sheet-pile toe extends 0.5 ft into the SW-GW stratum below El. 720.0 so that the tips bear below the base of the clay,
as contemplated in Geotechnical Report Section 9.4. The penetration is nominal and the sheet-pile wall is not credited as a cutoff against
confined aquifer flow; the aquifer is continuous beneath the pit and is controlled by the relief wells of R2.1, and the sheet interlocks are sealed over
the aquitard interval in accordance with Geotechnical Report Section 9.6.

R2.5 — Tieback Ground Anchor Design (Supersedes Rev.1 Section 7)
Lateral support near the top of the sheet-pile wall is provided by a single row of multi-strand tieback ground anchors installed at waler elevation El.
745.5 at an inclination of 20° below horizontal and spaced horizontally at 6 ft centres. Each ground anchor is detailed with a 25 ft free length and
a 24 ft bond length (49 ft total anchor length).




                          KE-L-2026-0713 | Submittal 31-SH-B Rev.2 | Birchwood Village Expansion Program, Package A | Page 3 of 5
 R2.5 — Tieback Ground Anchor Design (Continued)
 • Design Anchor Load at 6 ft Centres: Crediting the allowable passive toe resistance (Pp,allow = 16,211 / 1.50 = 10,807 lb/ft) against the total
   horizontal driving load of 19,610 lb/ft (Section R2.3), the required horizontal anchor reaction is Th = 19,610 − 10,807 = 8,803 lb/ft. For anchors
   spaced at 6 ft centres and inclined at 20° below horizontal, the design anchor working load is:
    Tdesign = (8,803 lb/ft × 6.0 ft) / cos 20° = 52,818 lb / 0.93969 = 56,208 lb = 56.2 kips
 • Anchor Bond Capacity: The 24 ft bond length is formed by pressure-grouted tieback installation through a 6.0-in nominal diameter drill hole
   (dh = 6.0 in) at the design bond stress of 20 psi adopted in Rev.1 Section 10.4 (FHWA-IF-99-015, Table 4). Temporary drill casing is advanced
   and grouted over the aquitard interval to seal against artesian seepage during anchor installation. Ultimate bond capacity is:
     Qult = π × dh × Lb × τbond = π × 6.0 in × (24 ft × 12 in/ft) × 20 psi = 108,573 lb = 108.6 kips
 • Anchor Capacity Check: Comparing ultimate bond capacity of 108.6 kips against the design load of 56.2 kips at 6 ft centres yields a factor of
   safety of FSanchor = 108.6 / 56.2 = 1.93 (adequate on the adopted design bond stress of FHWA-IF-99-015, Table 4). The anchor tendon is
   unchanged from Rev.1 Section 10.1: (4) 0.6-in Grade 270 strand, design strength 140 kips against the 56.2 kip design load. Each anchor is
   proof tested to 1.33 × 56.2 = 74.8 kips and locked off at 0.75 × 56.2 = 42.2 kips. The proof load exceeds the design load by 33 per cent and is
   taken as the demonstration of anchor performance for the period the wall is in service.

R2.6 — Sheet-Pile Structural Bending Check (Supersedes Rev.1 Section 9)
The PZ-35 Grade 50 section adopted in Rev.1 Section 11.2 is retained and re-checked against the revised effective-stress plus hydrostatic lateral
loading (Fy = 50 ksi, elastic section modulus Sx = 48.5 in3/ft of wall).
 • Allowable Flexural Capacity (Mallow): At an allowable bending stress of Fb = 0.60 Fy = 30.0 ksi per AISC 360-16 Chapter F, as adopted in
   Rev.1 Section 11.2:
     Mallow = (Fb × Sx) / (12 in/ft) = (30.0 ksi × 48.5 in3/ft) / 12 = 121 kip-ft/ft
 • Maximum Span Bending Moment (Mmax): Under the Section R2.3 loading and El. 745.5 anchor reaction, the point of zero shear occurs at El.
   733.1, producing a maximum flexural demand of 62.4 kip-ft/ft.
 • Flexural Factor of Safety: FSflex = 121 kip-ft/ft / 62.4 kip-ft/ft = 1.94 ≥ 1.50 required (Rev.1 §11.2) (PZ-35 Grade 50 section is structurally
   adequate).

R2.7 — Wall Deflection & Piezometer Trigger (Supersedes Rev.1 Section 10)
Wall deflection is re-estimated by the method of Rev.1 Section 12.1 for the PZ-35 Grade 50 sheet-pile wall tied back at El. 745.5 under the revised
Section R2.3 loading, giving a predicted maximum lateral wall deflection of 1.3 in at El. 738.0.
 • Allowable Deflection Criterion: For exposed excavation height H = 24.0 ft = 288 in, the criterion adopted in Rev.1 Section 12.3 is H/200 = 1.44
    in (δmax = 1.3 in < H/200 = 1.44 in — OK).
 • Instrumentation & Construction Action Limit: Active construction monitoring of piezometers VW-B1 through VW-B3 shall enforce a
    mandatory stop-work trigger if the piezometers read above El. 727.0 during excavation below El. 732.0 (in addition to the Section R2.1
    72-hour confirmation hold). If any piezometer reading exceeds El. 727.0, excavation operations shall cease immediately until relief-well pumping
    restores piezometric head to or below El. 726.5.

   SECTION 1 — DESIGN BASIS
   1.1 General
   These calculations establish the design of the temporary support of excavation for the deep plant-room excavation
   planned beneath Block B of Package A of the Birchwood Village Expansion Program. The excavation is a
   rectangular pit approximately 68 ft × 44 ft in plan, cut into the podium footprint east of the shared Block A/B
   basement. Excavation commences from a working grade at El. 750.0 and terminates at a plant-room subgrade at
   El. 726.0, a total excavated depth of 24 ft.
   The temporary works described herein are the Contractor's means and methods and are supplied by delegated
   design under Article 3.1.B of Specification Section 31 50 00.

   1.2 Selected System
   A driven steel sheet-pile wall, restrained by a single row of pre-stressed tieback anchors installed near the top of
   the excavation, has been selected as the support system. The rationale is:
      • (a) The excavation is deeper than would be economically supported by a cantilever wall;
      • (b) A single-level tied wall provides adequate stiffness for the 24 ft depth without a soldier-pile / lagging
      system, and drives to competent stratigraphy without an oversized toe;
      • (c) A continuous sheet-pile section provides a substantially closed perimeter and does not rely on open-face
      lagging.
   Timber lagging with soldier piles was evaluated and rejected for this reason.

   1.3 Geometry — Adopted Design Values
    Parameter                                       Symbol           Value                   Reference
    Working grade (behind wall)                     Elev_wg          El. 750.0 ft            S-101 (Foundation Plan, Rev.4)

    Plant-room subgrade (inside wall)               Elev_sg          El. 726.0 ft            S-101 (Foundation Plan, Rev.4)

    Total excavated depth                           H                24 ft                   Elev_wg − Elev_sg
    Sheet-pile tip (toe) elevation                  Elev_toe         El. 722.0 ft            Design adopted herein
    Sheet-pile total length (cutoff El. 750.0 to toe) L_sp           28 ft                   (750.0 − 722.0)
    Embedment below subgrade                        D                4 ft                    (726.0 − 722.0)
    Tieback anchor row elevation                    Elev_tb          El. 745.5 ft            Design adopted herein
    Excavation plan dimensions                      —                68 ft × 44 ft           S-101 (Foundation Plan, Rev.4)


   The sheet-pile toe at El. 722.0 lies within the CL clay aquitard described in Section 3, and above the top of the
   underlying dense sand and gravel stratum. The wall is therefore driven and toed entirely within cohesive
   stratigraphy.

   1.4 Design Codes and References
        • IBC 2021 (Ohio Building Code adoption) — general design requirements;
        • AISC 360-16 — structural steel design of sheet-pile section;
        • U.S. Steel Sheet Piling Design Manual (1984 ed.) and USACE EM 1110-2-2504 — sheet-pile wall design
        methodology;
        • FHWA Ground Anchors and Anchored Systems Manual (FHWA-IF-99-015) — tieback design;
        • ASCE 7-16 — construction loads and surcharge.

   1.5 Delegated Design Statement

   SECTION 3 — SUBSURFACE CONDITIONS AND SOIL PARAMETERS
   3.1 Stratigraphy
   The subsurface profile in the Block B plant-room excavation footprint is taken from the Geotechnical Report
   (R-1), specifically borings B-04 and B-06, which fall within the footprint, and borings B-07 and B-08 adjacent to
   the basement mat. The profile adopted for design is summarized as follows:

   Stratum                                Elevation Range                      USCS          Description
   Engineered structural fill                                                                Compacted granular fill placed
                                          El. 750.0 to El. 738.0               —
   (Block B footprint)                                                                       over stripped clay, 10–11/2025
   Upper Sand                             Absent beneath Block B               SP-SM         Present over Blocks A and C only
                                                                                             Normally-consolidated, medium
   Compressible Clay Aquitard             El. 738.0 to El. 720.0               CL
                                                                                             plasticity clay, 18 ft thick
   Deep Sand and Gravel                   Below El. 720.0                      SW-GW         Dense sand and gravel

   The full 24 ft of excavation from El. 750.0 to El. 726.0 removes the engineered fill and the upper 12 ft of the CL
   clay aquitard. The sheet-pile toe at El. 722.0 sits within the CL clay stratum, 2 ft above its base.

   3.2 Soil Design Properties
   The design values below are adopted from the Geotechnical Report (R-1), Section 6 and Table 6.2, together with
   the total unit weights carried forward on the Design Basis Memorandum (R-6) as governing profile values.

                     Stratum                       γ_total (pcf)    φ' (deg)         c' (psf)      s_u (psf)          Ka        Kp
   Engineered Fill (SP-SM)                              118            32               0              —             0.307      3.25

   12 ft clay)

   3.3 Design Approach — Blended Profile
   For the calculation of the active pressure diagram behind the wall from working grade El. 750.0 down to
   subgrade El. 726.0, a blended profile is adopted using a weighted average total unit weight of 119 pcf and an
   equivalent effective friction angle of 30° (giving Ka = 0.333, Kp = 3.00). The blended profile provides a
   conservative envelope that:
       • (a) does not credit any cohesion contribution from the clay,
       • (b) treats both strata as frictional with a single unified Ka, and
       • (c) reproduces the vertical stress at subgrade within 1% of the layered calculation.
   This is a standard simplification for the design of temporary sheet-pile walls of this proportion. The
   blended-profile assumption is checked against a layered calculation in Section 5.3.

   3.4 Groundwater Assumption for the Design Case
   Per Section 2 above, and consistent with Reference R-3 (Contractor's dewatering plan, Submittal 31-DW-A), the
   excavation is to be drawn down per Contractor's dewatering plan. Accordingly, the design case treated in
   these calculations assumes dry conditions from working grade El. 750.0 down to subgrade El. 726.0 for the
   duration of the temporary works. No pore water pressure is carried in the active or passive earth-pressure
   diagrams below.

   SECTION 4 — DESIGN LOADS AND SURCHARGE
   4.1 Surcharge
   The following surcharges are applied at the ground surface at El. 750.0 behind the wall:

  Source                                               Magnitude              Type          Extent
  Construction traffic, laydown, and light equipment   q_c = 250 psf          Uniform       Continuous behind wall
  Adopted nominal live load allowance                  q_L = 100 psf          Uniform       Continuous behind wall
  Total design surcharge                               q = 250 psf            Uniform       Governing

   The 250 psf construction surcharge governs and is carried as a uniform load applied at the ground surface
   throughout the calculation. Point loads from heavy equipment (haul trucks, mobile cranes) are excluded from the
   perimeter zone within 10 ft of the wall by operational restriction; this restriction is to be reflected in the site
   logistics plan and enforced by the Superintendent.

   4.2 Lateral Pressure from Surcharge
   Under Rankine theory with a uniform surface surcharge, the additional horizontal pressure applied to the wall is:
         p_q = Ka · q = 0.333 · 250 = 83 psf
   This 83 psf is constant with depth over the retained height (rectangular distribution, top to subgrade).

   4.3 Water-Bearing Load
   No water-bearing lateral pressure is included in the active pressure diagram, because groundwater within the
   excavation footprint is to be drawn down per the Contractor's dewatering plan (Reference R-3, Submittal
   31-DW-A) prior to and throughout excavation. The design case is dry above subgrade El. 726.0.

   4.4 Other Loads
   No adjacent building loads are within the zone of influence of the excavation; the nearest permanent structure is
   the Blocks A/B basement mat, whose exterior face is beyond the 1H:1V influence line from the wall. No seismic
   case is required for a temporary support of excavation of this duration (< 6 months planned).




Birchwood Village Expansion Program — Package A                                                                      Page 7
 Kesterline Engineering, PC                                Submittal 31-SH-B | Rev.1 | Block B Plant-Room Shoring Calculations




   SECTION 5 — LATERAL EARTH PRESSURE — ACTIVE SIDE
   5.1 Method
   Rankine active earth pressure theory is applied, with the blended profile per Section 3.3. The wall is assumed
   vertical, the ground surface horizontal, no wall friction, and no water-bearing pressure (per Section 4.3).

   5.2 Active Earth Pressure Distribution
   Adopted parameters:
       • γ_blended = 119 pcf
       • φ' = 30°, Ka = 0.333
       • Retained height H = 24 ft (El. 750.0 to El. 726.0)
       • Surcharge q = 250 psf
   At any depth z below the ground surface (measured downward from El. 750.0):
         p_a(z) = Ka · γ · z + Ka · q
                    = 0.333 · 119 · z + 0.333 · 250
                    = 39.6 · z + 83          [psf, z in ft]
   At the subgrade (z = 24 ft, El. 726.0):
        • Component from soil weight: 0.333 · 119 · 24 = 951 psf ≈ 950 psf
        • Component from surcharge: 0.333 · 250 = 83 psf
        • Total active pressure at subgrade: 950 + 83 = 1,033 psf
   The 950 psf effective lateral pressure at subgrade is the earth-pressure component and is the value carried forward
   as the governing lateral pressure at the excavated bottom under the drawn-down condition established in Section
   2 and Section 4.3.
   Design active pressure diagram (behind wall, El. 750.0 down to El. 726.0):
         El. 750.0      ____________
                        |     83 psf (surcharge rectangle)

                        |              \
                        |               \
                        |                 \
         El. 726.0      |________________\_____
                                           1,033 psf total

   5.3 Layered Check
   For verification of the blended-profile simplification, a layered calculation is carried out below (engineered fill
   El. 750–738 with Ka_fill = 0.307, γ_fill = 118 pcf; clay El. 738–726 with Ka_clay = 0.390, γ_clay = 120 pcf,
   cohesion neglected).

        12+ ft        738.0 (top of clay)                1,416                0.390                   552

         24 ft               726.0                    2,856                0.390                  1,114

   The layered check yields 1,114 psf earth-pressure component at subgrade. The blended-profile calculation at 950

   envelope. The blended envelope is confirmed to be a reasonable simplification for wall design, with the layered
   case treated in the toe-embedment sizing.

   5.4 Governing Design Value
   Design lateral earth pressure at subgrade El. 726.0: 950 psf
   This is the value at which the sheet-pile section, tieback design, and toe-embedment check are governed in the
   sections that follow.

   SECTION 6 — LATERAL EARTH PRESSURE — PASSIVE SIDE
   6.1 Passive Resistance Below Subgrade
   Below the subgrade at El. 726.0 and down to the sheet-pile toe at El. 722.0, passive earth pressure is mobilized on
   the inside face of the wall. The stratum is CL clay throughout this 4-ft interval. The design passive pressure is
   computed using the long-term drained parameters (φ' = 26°, Kp = 2.56, c' = 100 psf), which is conservative
   relative to the short-term undrained case for the anticipated 4- to 5-month duration of the temporary works.
   At depth d below subgrade (d in ft):
         p_p(d) = Kp · γ · d + 2 · c' · √Kp
                   = 2.56 · 120 · d + 2 · 100 · √2.56
                   = 307 · d + 320          [psf, d in ft]
   At the toe (d = 4 ft, El. 722.0):
         p_p(toe) = 307 · 4 + 320 = 1,228 + 320 = 1,548 psf
   Design passive pressure diagram (in front of wall, El. 726.0 down to El. 722.0):
         El. 726.0           _______
                             |        320 psf (cohesion rectangle)
                             |___________

                                           \

   6.2 Design Passive Force per Foot of Wall
   Passive force per lineal foot of wall over the 4 ft embedment:
       • Rectangular (cohesion) contribution: 320 · 4 = 1,280 lb/ft
       • Triangular (frictional) contribution: 0.5 · (1,548 − 320) · 4 = 2,456 lb/ft
       • Total mobilizable passive resistance: P_p = 3,736 lb/ft ≈ 3,740 lb/ft

   6.3 Reduction Factor
   A factor of safety of 1.5 is applied to the mobilizable passive resistance for the design case (temporary works,
   the delegated designer’s adopted criteria):
         P_p,design = P_p / 1.5 = 3,740 / 1.5 = 2,493 lb/ft ≈ 2,490 lb/ft

       1. Block C — Spread footings may be founded within the upper sand. Consolidation of the underlying

       2. Blocks A and B basement mat — A conventional reinforced-concrete mat foundation may be founded

       3. Block B piles — Because of anticipated fill-induced consolidation of the underlying clay and the
       resulting downdrag loads, and because column loads at Block B exceed the safe capacity of shallow
       foundations bearing on the upper sand, closed-end driven pipe piles carried through the upper sand and the
       clay to bearing in the dense sand and gravel aquifer below El. 720.0 are recommended. The pile design
       must address soil-pile interaction from clay consolidation, as the engineered fill load induces downdrag on
       piles driven through the consolidating clay (Section 8.3).
       4. Block B plant-room excavation — The plant-room subgrade is planned near El. 726.0, i.e., inside the
       clay aquitard, approximately 6 ft above the top of the confined aquifer at El. 720.0. Because the confined
       piezometric head (El. 738.0) is approximately 12 ft above the planned subgrade elevation, this excavation
       will develop a significant uplift pressure on the clay plug from the underlying aquifer.
       The base-heave stability of the plug must be evaluated by the design team, and pressure-relief
       or aquifer-drawdown measures may be required. This condition is called out as the controlling
       constructability issue for the plant-room excavation and must be addressed by the Contractor’s dewatering
       and shoring designs.
       5. Engineered fill over the clay — The 12 ft of engineered fill required beneath Block B (from El. 738.0
       up to El. 750.0) will constitute a net surcharge on the normally-consolidated compressible clay across the
       Block B footprint. Because σ'p ≈ σ'0, the entire increment is virgin compression under Cc. The Owner is
       advised that consolidation of the underlying clay under this fill surcharge will occur, that the associated
       settlement will affect the behavior of any deep foundations driven from the raised working grade before
       the consolidation is substantially complete, and that these effects must be considered in the pile design.


 This Rev.2 supersedes Rev.1 dated 12/12/2024 in its entirety.


 2. INTRODUCTION AND SCOPE

 2.1 Authorization
 Authorization for the geotechnical investigation was issued by Thornbury State University, Office of Capital
 Programs, under Kelbrook Geotechnical Proposal P-2024-116 dated September 6, 2024, and Notice-to-Proceed
 dated October 1, 2024. Field exploration commenced 10/28/2024 and was completed 11/22/2024. Laboratory
 testing was performed between 11/2024 and 01/2025 by Vantree Materials Testing, LLC (Vantree) under
 separate contract to the Owner. Groundwater monitoring readings taken through 02/03/2025 are incorporated in
 this Rev.2 issue; monitoring is ongoing and will continue during construction.

 2.2 Project Description
 Package A of the Birchwood Village Expansion Program consists of three student-housing blocks:
      • Block A — six-story residential tower over a shared podium, seated on a basement mat foundation.
      • Block B — six-story residential tower over a shared podium, seated on the same basement mat
      foundation as Block A, with a separate deep plant-room excavation planned in the southwest quadrant of
      the block footprint (elevator and mechanical/electrical service space, approximately 24 ft below design
      grade).
      • Block C — six-story residential tower over the shared podium, on spread footings; no basement is
      planned beneath Block C.


Kelbrook Geotechnical, Inc. | 1120 Kinnear Road, Columbus, Ohio 43212 | (614) 555-0204                         Page 7
 Kelbrook Project No. KGI-2024-0417                          Birchwood Village Package A — Geotechnical Report — Rev.2


 The shared podium is a one-story reinforced-concrete transfer structure below the residential towers. Finished
 design grade at the podium top is established at El. 750.0 ft. Underside of the basement mat beneath Blocks A
 and B is set at approximately El. 731.5 ft. The plant-room excavation beneath Block B is planned to reach
 subgrade at approximately El. 726.0 ft.

 2.3 Purpose and Scope of Investigation
 The purpose of the investigation was to:
      • Characterize the subsurface soil profile, groundwater conditions and hydrogeologic regime across the
      Package A footprint;
      • Recover and test representative undisturbed samples of the compressible clay stratum in order to develop
      consolidation parameters for foundation-settlement analysis;
      • Provide geotechnical recommendations for the foundation of each block, for the design of the basement
      mat and the plant-room excavation, and for the engineered fill required to bring the Block B footprint to
      design grade; and
      • Provide construction considerations for dewatering, temporary excavation support and site preparation.
 The scope of work comprised:
      • Nine (9) soil borings, B-01 through B-09, drilled to depths ranging 55 to 90 ft below existing ground

 3.1 Site Location and Topography
 The Package A site is located at 1802 Larchwood Avenue, on the western portion of the Thornbury State
 University main campus in Columbus, Ohio. The site is bounded to the north by Larchwood Avenue, to the east
 by an existing campus surface parking lot, to the south by an unimproved landscaped strip and to the west by an
 existing academic building. The overall Package A footprint is approximately 3.7 acres.
 Existing topography varies substantially across            Ground surface stands at approximately El. 750.0 ft
 across the footprints of Blocks A and C in the northern and eastern portions of           Toward the southwest,
 across the footprint of Block B, ground surface falls to about El. 738.0 ft (a difference of about 12 ft) in what
 appears from historical aerial photography to have been a surface drainage swale draining the pre-development
 ground westward toward a former off-site low area. The transition between the two elevations is gradual across
 a nominal 60 to 80 ft width. Existing ground within Block B is generally covered with a thin (~0.5 to 1 ft)
 mantle of soft organic-rich silty topsoil overlying the SP-SM upper sand; no fill of engineering significance is
 present beneath Block B in its current condition.

 3.2 Regional and Local Geology
 Columbus, Ohio lies within the Till Plains section of the Central Lowland physiographic province. Regional
 surficial geology is dominated by Wisconsinan-age glacial deposits — chiefly clay-rich till, glaciolacustrine silt
 and clay, and outwash sand and gravel — overlying Devonian-age carbonate and shale bedrock. Local
 hydrogeology is characterized by a shallow phreatic surface within the outwash and reworked outwash sands, a
 laterally continuous fine-grained aquitard, and a lower confined aquifer within basal outwash sand and gravel
 above bedrock.
 The subsurface conditions encountered in the Package A borings are consistent with this regional framework: a
 medium-dense reworked outwash sand at the surface, a low-permeability clay of glaciolacustrine origin at
 intermediate depth, and a dense outwash sand and gravel aquifer at depth. Bedrock was not encountered within
 the maximum boring depth of 90 ft (approximately El. 660.0). Blow counts in the SW-GW below El. 720.0
 were consistently in the range N ≥ 50 blows per 6 inches, indicating a very dense sand-and-gravel deposit
 suitable as a pile-bearing stratum.

 3.3 Site History and Prior Use
 Site historical review — including review of Franklin County parcel records, USGS topographic maps (1955
 and later editions), and Thornbury State University campus master planning archives — indicates that the
 Package A parcel was in agricultural use through approximately 1958, was acquired by the University in 1962,
 and has been used for surface parking and landscape maintenance since. No prior structures of consequence, no
 known below-grade utilities (other than a single abandoned 6-inch clay drain traced along the historic swale in
 Block B), and no known industrial fill are present within the footprint. Because there is essentially no prior fill
 of engineering significance, the Block B footprint requires new engineered fill — placed on the natural
 clay-upper-sand contact after removal of the topsoil mantle — to bring the site to design grade.

 8.1 Consolidation of the Clay Aquitard

 the standard one-dimensional consolidation equation, in which Sc is the settlement and q the stress increase:
         Sc   = Cc · H / (1 + e0) · log10[ (σ'0 + q) / σ'0 ]

      • Cc = 0.28
      • e0 = 0.92

 8.3 Downdrag on Deep Foundations



 The Block B footprint is raised approximately 12 ft above its natural surface by engineered fill placed
 over a normally-consolidated CLAY 18 ft thick and of low permeability. Primary consolidation of that
 clay under the weight of the new fill was in progress at the date of this issue and, on the coefficients
 measured in the laboratory series, is expected to continue for a period measured in years rather than
 months.

 Deep foundations driven from the raised working grade pass through that consolidating layer. Where the
 surrounding soil settles more than the pile, the relative movement at the pile-soil interface reverses:
 the soil moves down past the shaft instead of the shaft moving down past the soil.


 Over the depth in which that condition applies the interface shear acts downward on the pile. It is an
 additional axial load carried by the pile, not a component of its resistance, and it is superimposed on
 the structural load for as long as consolidation continues.
 The magnitude depends on the thickness of the still-consolidating layer, the interface shear available
 within it and the depth of the neutral plane. Requirements for its treatment in design are set out in
 Section 9.3.

 upper SP-SM sand; and (c) settlement of a shallow foundation on the upper sand would be governed by
 consolidation of the underlying clay, deep foundations are recommended at Block B.
 Recommended pile type: Closed-end driven steel pipe piles, driven through the engineered fill, the upper sand,
 and the CL clay to bearing in the dense SW-GW sand and gravel aquifer below El. 720.0. The tip elevation is to
 be selected by the Structural Engineer of Record to develop the required end-bearing resistance and to satisfy
 the geotechnical capacity check at that tip, using conventional static analysis (Meyerhof, Nordlund or
 equivalent method) with an appropriate factor of safety against ultimate axial resistance. Driving will be
 verified with a wave-equation analysis, dynamic testing on the first production pile per block, and pile-driving
 records for every pile.
 Axial demand on the pile must include the anticipated
 downdrag load computed by the neutral-plane method for the clay stratum (and for the engineered fill above it,
 if consolidation of the fill and of the clay is not substantially complete at the time of pile installation). Because
 the engineered fill will be placed shortly before pile driving in the anticipated schedule, and because the
 coefficient of consolidation of the CL clay indicates a primary-consolidation time on the order of years,

 Working grade for driving: Piles are anticipated to be driven from the raised working grade at El. 750.0 (i.e.,

 9.4 Block B Plant-Room Excavation
 The plant-room excavation is planned to reach subgrade at approximately El. 726.0, which lies within the CL
 clay approximately 6 ft above the top of the confined SW-GW aquifer at El. 720.0. The confined piezometric
 head in the aquifer is at El. 738.0 (Section 7.2), i.e., approximately 12 ft above the planned subgrade.
 This excavation will develop confined-aquifer uplift on the clay plug that separates the subgrade from the
 aquifer (Section 8.2). The clay-plug residual thickness of only 6 ft is not, on its own, sufficient to resist the
 uplift pressure with an adequate factor of safety against base heave . Design mitigation is required. Options that
 the design team should evaluate include, individually or in combination:
      • Pressure-relief wells screened in the aquifer at or immediately outside the excavation footprint, pumped
      to reduce the piezometric head at the excavation subgrade elevation to a value that provides an adequate
      factor of safety against base heave for the intended excavation duration;
      • Deeper temporary sheeting with toe embedment penetrating into or through the clay and into the
      aquifer, so as to cut off inflow and confine the flow field around the sheeting toe;
      • Staged excavation or temporary ballast to preserve resisting weight against uplift during periods of
      exposure;
      • Alternative subgrade elevation, if any is available in the plant-room programming.
 The Contractor’s dewatering plan and the shoring design (both delegated designs) must together demonstrate an
 adequate factor of safety against base heave at the planned subgrade elevation, throughout the planned
 excavation duration, using the confined piezometric head El. 738.0 and the parameters in this report.




 9.5 Engineered Fill Placement over the Clay
 Bringing the Block B footprint to design grade requires placement of engineered fill of nominal 12 ft thickness
 (from natural ground at El. 738.0 up to design grade at El. 750.0). Because there is no substantial engineered fill
 or naturally overconsolidated material above the clay at Block B, the engineered fill is placed directly on the
 stripped clay surface after topsoil removal only.
 The engineered fill loads the underlying normally-consolidated CL clay as an areal surcharge, and consolidation
 of the clay under the fill surcharge will occur. Under the parameters of Table 5-1, the settlement caused by 12 ft
 of fill placed as a wide, essentially areal surcharge is substantial and will accrue over a period on the order of
 years. The engineering consequences must be reconciled by the design team:
      • If the fill is placed and given time to allow the underlying clay to substantially complete primary
      consolidation before piles are driven and the podium is erected, then the residual downdrag on the piles
      (and the residual differential settlement of any structure bearing at grade) is minimized. This is the
      preferred sequence.

      an added load.      Downdrag load contributions from the still-consolidating clay must be included

 Requirements for the fill material itself — gradation, compaction, moisture window, layer thickness and testing

 9.6 Dewatering, Excavation and Construction Considerations
      • The basement excavation for Blocks A and B, with a subgrade at approximately El. 731.5, is above the
      top of the clay (El. 738.0) and above the confined head (El. 738.0), but it is below the shallow water table
      (El. 742.0). Dewatering to control the shallow water table will be required in the upper sand around the
      basement excavation but will not reduce the confined head in the deep aquifer, and is not by itself a
      mitigation for the plant-room base-heave problem.
      • The confined-aquifer condition and the aquitard behavior of the CL clay must be preserved. Any activity
      that penetrates the clay across the plant-room footprint — including piles, pressure-relief wells, or shoring
      elements — must be sealed at the aquitard elevation so as not to short-circuit the aquitard.
      • Temporary sheeting design is a delegated design and is not scoped in this report; however, the shoring
      designer must be furnished with the confined head El. 738.0, the shallow water table El. 742.0, and the
      strength parameters and unit weights of each stratum for use in the shoring calculations.
      • Dewatering discharge is subject to Ohio EPA NPDES permitting requirements.
      Discharge quality (turbidity, TSS) and discharge quantity (rate, volume) will need to be permitted by the
      Contractor as part of the dewatering plan.

 5. SUMMARY
 Design water table adopted El. 742.0 ft; confined piezometric head El. 738.0 ft — both stable across monitoring
 period.

 The shallow SP-SM upper sand hosts an unconfined phreatic surface centered on El. 742.0, with all 57 individual
 shallow-piezometer readings (three piezometers × 19 rounds) falling within El. 741.6 to El. 742.4 across the 19-month
 monitoring period. The confined SW-GW sand and gravel aquifer below El. 720.0 exhibits a piezometric head centered on
 El. 738.0, with all 38 individual deep-piezometer readings (two piezometers × 19 rounds) falling within El. 737.7 to El.
 738.3 across the same period. The 18-ft-thick CL clay aquitard from El. 738.0 down to El. 720.0 separates the two
 regimes, and the two regimes have behaved independently across the monitoring record without evidence of hydraulic
 short-circuiting through the aquitard.

 1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

 Kelbrook Geotechnical, Inc. has completed a subsurface investigation and geotechnical engineering analysis for
 Package A of the Birchwood Village Expansion Program at 1802 Larchwood Avenue, Columbus, Ohio.
 Package A comprises three student-housing blocks (Blocks A, B and C) constructed over a shared podium, with
 a single basement level beneath Blocks A and B, and a separate deep plant-room excavation planned beneath
 Block B.
 The finished design grade across Package A is established at El. 750.0 ft. Existing ground surface stands at
 approximately El. 750.0 across the footprints of Blocks A and C but falls to about El. 738.0 across the Block B
 footprint (a former surface drainage swale). Placement of engineered fill of variable thickness — up to
 approximately 12 ft beneath Block B — will therefore be required to bring the site to design grade.
 The subsurface profile consists of three principal strata:
      • Stratum 1 — Upper sand, classified SP-SM (poorly-graded sand with silt), medium-dense, from
      existing grade down to El. 738.0, total unit weight 118 pcf.
      • Stratum 2 — Compressible clay aquitard, classified CL (lean clay of medium plasticity),
      normally-consolidated, from El. 738.0 down to El. 720.0 (18 ft thick), total unit weight 120 pcf, low
      permeability. This is the strata governing settlement of shallow foundations and provides the aquitard
      between the shallow and deep groundwater regimes.
      • Stratum 3 — Dense sand and gravel aquifer, classified SW-GW, below El. 720.0, total unit weight 130
      pcf, confined by the overlying clay.
 Groundwater is present as two distinct regimes:
      • The design water table in the upper sand is set at El. 742.0 ft. Piezometer readings taken from three
      shallow standpipes over the 11/2024–02/2025 monitoring period range from El. 741.6 to El. 742.4;
      groundwater seepage was observed at El. 741.8 to El. 742.2 in the Block A test-pit excavation.
      • A confined piezometric head of El. 738.0 ft has been measured in the deep sand-and-gravel aquifer
      through two deep piezometers screened below El. 720.0, with readings ranging El. 737.7 to El. 738.3. The
      confined head is at essentially the same elevation as the top of the clay aquitard.
 Consolidation testing on two undisturbed Shelby-tube samples of the compressible clay (samples B-06 U3 and
 B-08 U2, tested per ASTM D2435) yielded a compression index Cc = 0.28, a recompression index Cr = 0.045,
 an initial void ratio e0 = 0.92, an in-situ vertical effective stress σ'0 = 1,850 psf, and a preconsolidation pressure
 σ'p = 1,900 psf. The margin (σ'p − σ'0 ≈ 50 psf) confirms the clay is essentially normally-consolidated: any net
 stress increase applied at the top of the clay will produce virgin (Cc) compression rather than recompression
 (Cr) compression.
 Principal geotechnical recommendations are as follows:
       1. Block C — Spread footings may be founded within the upper sand. Consolidation of the underlying
       compressible clay under column-load stress increases at mid-depth of the clay must be explicitly computed

cc:                  Mr. Rahul Nimkar — Thelbridge Project Management Services (Geotechnical Reviewer)
cc:                  Mr. Gregory Nash, PE — Calloway Braddock Structural Engineers, LLC (EOR)


 1. Purpose and Scope
 This field observation report documents excavation observations, groundwater monitoring readings and seepage
 observations recorded by Kelbrook Geotechnical field personnel across the Package A footprint over the
 construction period 07/2025 through 05/2026. The observations reported herein are drawn from the writer’s
 daily field notes, from the shallow standpipe and deep piezometer monitoring log maintained under the ongoing
 Package A groundwater monitoring program, and from photographs and sketches taken at the time of
 observation. The report is furnished in support of the Owner’s Representative construction verification file and
 as supplemental record to the Geotechnical Investigation Report Rev.2 (KGI-2024-0417).
 Two distinct field episodes are documented: (a) the Block A basement excavation, opened in the summer of
 2025 to a working subgrade at approximately El. 730.0; and (b) the placement of engineered fill across the
 Block B footprint from 10/06/2025 through 11/02/2025 and the subsequent months of pile installation and
 lift-up to design grade. Groundwater monitoring is continuous across both episodes and is reported in full.

 2. Excavation Observations — Block A Basement
 2.1 Excavation Opening and Progression




Field Observation Report — Excavation and Groundwater — Package A                                             Page 1
 Kelbrook Geotechnical, Inc.                                                                                     Report No. KGI-FO-2026-0528




 The Block A basement excavation was opened in the northeast quadrant of the Package A footprint on
 07/14/2025 and progressed from existing grade El. 750.0 down to a working subgrade at approximately El.
 730.0 (approximately one foot below the design underside of the basement mat at El. 731.5, to accommodate a
 lean-concrete working mat). The excavation was carried out by the Contractor using a mid-size hydraulic
 excavator with side dumping to trucks; sequence proceeded from the east perimeter westward across the Block
 A footprint over the course of approximately three weeks.
 Perimeter shoring — a combination of soldier pile and timber lagging along the northern and eastern faces, and
 open-cut battered slopes along the interior (Block A / Block B transition) — was installed ahead of the cut face.
 Well-point dewatering, executed per the Contractor’s Dewatering and Groundwater Control Plan Rev.1
 dated 06/04/2025, was activated on 07/12/2025, two days before the first cut, and remained in operation
 continuously through mat placement on 01/12/2026 and thereafter to protect the wall pour sequence.

 2.2 Side Conditions Observed in the Cut Face
 Exposed cut faces along the Block A perimeter revealed the following, consistent with the strata described in
 Section 6 of the reference report:
   •    From existing grade El. 750.0 down to approximately El. 746.0: approximately 4 ft of loose topsoil,
        root-mat and reworked surface fill of engineering significance limited to the upper 0.5 to 1 ft, transitioning
        downward into weathered upper sand. This layer was over-excavated and hauled off-site as unsuitable for
        structural fill re-use.
   •    From approximately El. 746.0 down to El. 738.0: the SP-SM upper sand — medium-dense, moist above
        the water table and saturated below it, with a modest silt content and no interbedded fine-grained seams.
        Cut face stability in the sand above the water table was satisfactory at 1H:1V; below the water table (once
        dewatered) the face was cut vertically against the shoring without slumping.
   •    From El. 738.0 down to the working subgrade at El. 730.0: the top of the CL clay aquitard, exposed as
        a stiff, medium-plasticity lean clay of grey-brown colour. The top of the clay at El. 738.0 was consistent
        within ± 0.5 ft across the Block A footprint. The clay retained a vertical or near-vertical face for the
        excavation duration without noticeable creep or heave; subgrade compaction footprint (proof-rolling)
        produced no rutting or pumping under the loaded haul truck used for the check.
 The transition from Stratum 1 (upper sand) to Stratum 2 (clay) at El. 738.0 was sharp and well-defined in the cut
 face and matched the elevation logged in Borings B-01, B-02, B-07 and B-09 within a few tenths of a foot.

 2.3 Working Subgrade Condition
 Subgrade at El. 730.0 was inspected on 08/06/2025 in the presence of the Contractor’s Superintendent (Mr.
 Marcus Whitfield) and the Owner’s Representative (Mr. Adrian Vance      ). Subgrade was found to be firm,
 uniform, free of standing water within the dewatered footprint, and suitable to receive the lean-concrete
 working mat and subsequently the reinforced mat foundation. No soft spots, disturbed zones or unsuitable
 inclusions were logged. The subgrade approval memorandum was issued separately by Kelbrook on
 08/07/2025.

 3. Groundwater Monitoring — Continuous Record
 Groundwater monitoring under the Package A program continues from the piezometer array installed
 11/22/2024 and reported in the Geotechnical Investigation Report Rev.2. Over the observation period 07/2025
 through 05/2026 an additional eleven monitoring rounds were completed, bringing the total record to eighteen

 rounds since installation. Readings are taken monthly (weekly during active excavation and dewatering).



Field Observation Report — Excavation and Groundwater — Package A                                                                    Page 2
 Kelbrook Geotechnical, Inc.                                                               Report No. KGI-FO-2026-0528




 3.1 Design Water Table — Upper Sand (Shallow Standpipe Piezometers)
 The design water table in the upper SP-SM sand, established at El. 742.0 in the reference report, is confirmed
 by the extended monitoring record. Readings from the three shallow standpipe piezometers (B-01, B-03, B-09),
 taken across the 07/2025 through 05/2026 observation period at locations outside the Block A dewatered
 footprint, remain in the range El. 741.6 to El. 742.4, with individual monthly means clustered within a few
 tenths of a foot of El. 742.0. No systematic trend, no seasonal excursion beyond that range and no departure
 from the design elevation was recorded.

 3.2 Confined Piezometric Head — Deep Aquifer (Deep Piezometers)
 The confined piezometric head in the deep SW-GW sand-and-gravel aquifer below El. 720.0, established at El.
 738.0 in the reference report, is likewise confirmed. Readings from the two deep piezometers (B-04 and B-08),
 both screened below El. 720.0 within the Block B footprint, remain in the range El. 737.7 to El. 738.3 across
 the full extended record. The head is stable, without trend, and consistent with the value carried forward from
 the Rev.2 investigation.

 3.3 Summary of Extended Monitoring Range
                                                                      Extended range            Representative
        Piezometer                       Screen zone
                                                                    (07/2025 – 05/2026)            reading

 B-01 (shallow standpipe)     Upper sand                             El. 741.7 – 742.3              El. 742.0

 B-03 (shallow standpipe)     Upper sand                             El. 741.6 – 742.4              El. 742.0

 B-09 (shallow standpipe)     Upper sand                             El. 741.8 – 742.2              El. 742.0

 B-04 (deep piezometer)       Deep aquifer (below El. 720.0)         El. 737.7 – 738.3              El. 738.0

 B-08 (deep piezometer)       Deep aquifer (below El. 720.0)         El. 737.8 – 738.2              El. 738.0

 Both regimes — the shallow phreatic surface at El. 742.0 in the upper sands and the confined piezometric head
 at El. 738.0 in the deep aquifer below El. 720.0 — remain consistent with KGI-2024-0417 Rev.2. The
 eighteen-foot separation between the top of the clay aquitard and the top of the deep aquifer continues to isolate
 the two regimes.

 4. Seepage Observations — Block A Excavation and Dewatering Response
 4.1 Seepage into the Cut Face
 During the Block A basement excavation, groundwater seepage was observed entering the excavation at the
 exposed cut face where the upper SP-SM sand was cut below the design water table. Seepage was concentrated
 at elevations El. 741.8 to El. 742.2, corresponding to the top of the phreatic surface in the upper sand. The
 seepage was clear (non-turbid after brief initial flushing), sustained rather than intermittent, and distributed
 along the cut face rather than emerging from a discrete conduit or seam. No seepage was observed emerging
 from the top of the CL clay at El. 738.0; the clay presented no visible cracks or fissures and no seepage exit
 points at or below its exposed face.
 The observed seepage elevations (El. 741.8 to El. 742.2) reproduce the range recorded in exploratory
 test-pitting during the original 2024 investigation and are consistent with the shallow standpipe piezometer
 readings from stations outside the dewatered footprint (Section 3.1). The two independent measurements —
 piezometer standpipe readings and cut-face seepage entry — corroborate each other and confirm the design
 water table elevation.



Field Observation Report — Excavation and Groundwater — Package A                                               Page 3
 Kelbrook Geotechnical, Inc.                                                               Report No. KGI-FO-2026-0528




 4.2 Well-Point Dewatering Response — Upper Sand
 Well-point dewatering, executed per the Contractor’s Dewatering and Groundwater Control Plan Rev.1
 was operated continuously across the Block A footprint from 07/12/2025 through the mat placement
 date and beyond. Piezometer readings taken from a spare standpipe drop set inside the dewatered perimeter, in
 combination with well-point riser inspections, showed the upper sand water level drawn down to approximately
 El. 728 within the dewatered perimeter — approximately 14 feet below the ambient design water table and
 approximately 2 feet below the working subgrade at El. 730.0. Drawdown within the perimeter was achieved
 within approximately 48 hours of well-point activation and was maintained at that level throughout the
 excavation and mat construction window.
 The dewatering system performed as designed for the shallow phreatic surface in the upper sand across the
 Block A footprint. Cut faces below the ambient water table, once well-point drawdown was established,
 presented no free seepage during the balance of the mat construction sequence.

 4.3 Deep Piezometer Response — Confirms Confined Aquifer Independence
 Deep piezometer readings from B-04 and B-08 (both screened in the deep SW-GW aquifer below El. 720.0 and
 located within the Block A / Block B footprint) were taken throughout the Block A dewatering campaign.
 Across the full period of well-point operation, both deep piezometers continued to read within the range El.
 737.7 to El. 738.3, with individual monthly means at or within a few tenths of El. 738.0.
 Deep piezometer readings within the Block A footprint were unaffected by upper-sand well-point dewatering.
 The upper sand and the deep aquifer are separated by the 18-ft-thick CL clay aquitard from El. 738.0 down to
 El. 720.0, and the well-point system draws only from the upper sand. The observed independence of the two
 regimes during active dewatering directly confirms the confined character of the deep aquifer and the aquitard
 behaviour of the clay, as characterized in the reference report.

 5. Notes on Block B — Engineered Fill Placement and Subsequent Monitoring
 5.1 Engineered Fill Placement, 10/06/2025 through 11/02/2025
 Engineered fill was placed across the Block B footprint over the period 10/06/2025 through 11/02/2025 to bring
 the site from natural ground at approximately El. 738.0 up to design grade at El. 750.0 — a nominal 12 ft of fill
 in 14 controlled lifts. Fill was placed directly on the stripped clay surface after removal of the surface topsoil
 mantle, in accordance with the recommendations of Section 9.5 of the reference report. Compaction and
 moisture control were performed under the independent Laboratory’s field density testing program (Vantree
 Materials Testing, LLC); the writer’s observations here are limited to the geotechnical monitoring associated
 with the underlying strata.

 5.2 Deep Piezometer Readings Through Fill Placement, Pile Driving and Subsequent Months
 The two deep piezometers B-04 and B-08 are located within the Block B footprint (B-04 within the plant-room
 excavation footprint, B-08 adjacent to the basement mat perimeter beneath Blocks A and B, both screened in
 the deep aquifer below El. 720.0). Both remained instrumented and readable through fill placement, through
 pile installation from 11/06/2025 through 11/21/2025, and through the subsequent months of the observation
 period.
 Across the entire sequence — before, during and after fill placement; before, during and after pile driving; and
 through the months following pile driving — deep piezometer readings continued to fall within the range El.
 737.7 to El. 738.3. Individual monthly means remained clustered at or within a few tenths of El. 738.0. No
 pumping, no departure from the ambient range, and no sustained response either to fill loading or to pile



Field Observation Report — Excavation and Groundwater — Package A                                              Page 4
 Kelbrook Geotechnical, Inc.                                                               Report No. KGI-FO-2026-0528




 installation was recorded in the deep-aquifer piezometers.
 The aquifer head re-establishes at El. 738.0 through the engineered fill placed above the clay; the fill does not
 alter the confined head, and the confined head does not respond to the fill load. This is expected behaviour for a
 laterally continuous confined aquifer isolated from the surface loading regime by an intact clay aquitard, and is
 reported here so that the record is complete.

 5.3 Shallow Standpipe Readings
 Shallow standpipe piezometer B-01 (Block A, outside the Block B fill footprint) and B-09 (Block C, outside the
 Block B fill footprint) continued to read within the El. 741.6 to El. 742.4 range through the fill-placement and
 pile-driving windows. Shallow standpipe B-03 (Block A / Block B transition) likewise continued in that range.
 The upper-sand phreatic surface at El. 742.0 outside the Block A dewatered footprint was not measurably
 affected by activity within the Block B fill footprint.

 6. Field Observation Summary
 The following observations are recorded for the observation period 07/2025 through 05/2026:
   1. The Block A basement excavation was opened in summer 2025 and carried to a working subgrade at
       approximately El. 730.0 (one foot below the design underside of the basement mat at El. 731.5). Cut faces
       exposed the upper SP-SM sand from grade to El. 738.0 and the top of the CL clay aquitard below.
       Subgrade condition on the clay was firm and suitable to receive the lean-concrete working mat.
   2. Seepage into the Block A cut face was observed at El. 741.8 to El. 742.2, coincident with the design water
       table El. 742.0 in the upper sand. No seepage was observed emerging from the top of the CL clay at El.
       738.0.

   1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE
   This memorandum establishes the governing codes, reference standards, site parameters, design loads, load
   combinations, and serviceability criteria adopted for the structural design of Package A of the Birchwood Village
   Expansion. Package A comprises three student-housing blocks (Blocks A, B and C) constructed over a shared
   podium, one basement level beneath Blocks A and B, and a separate deep plant-room excavation planned beneath
   Block B. The design basis stated herein governs all Package A calculations, drawings, and specifications issued
   by the Engineer of Record and controls the interpretation of subordinate design documents where a conflict
   arises.
   This Rev.2 issue supersedes Rev.1 dated 07/18/2025. Substantive changes since Rev.1 are recorded in the
   Revision Block on the final page.

   2. GOVERNING CODES AND REFERENCE STANDARDS

        code as adopted by the State of Ohio; Chapter 16 (Structural Design) references ASCE 7-16 for loads.
        • ACI 318-19, Building Code Requirements for Structural Concrete and Commentary — reinforced concrete
        design, detailing, cover, and serviceability.
        • ASCE 7-16, Minimum Design Loads and Associated Criteria for Buildings and Other Structures — dead,
        live, snow, wind, seismic loads and load combinations.
        • AISC 360-16, Specification for Structural Steel Buildings — structural steel members and connections at
        podium framing and roof.
        • ACI 301-20 for cast-in-place concrete construction requirements referenced through Spec 03 30 00.
        • ASCE 32-01 for frost-protected shallow foundations where applicable at Block C perimeter.
   Materials and test methods are governed by the specifications listed in Section 03 20 00, 03 30 00, and 31 20 00
   (Rev.2, current at the date of this memorandum), and where cited by ASTM designation on the drawings.
   Where an inconsistency arises between the Ohio Building Code (adopting IBC 2021) and a referenced consensus
   standard, the more stringent provision governs unless the Ohio amendment expressly modifies the standard.

   3. SITE CONDITIONS SUMMARY

   6. LOAD COMBINATIONS
   Strength design (LRFD) load combinations for gravity, wind, and seismic follow ASCE 7-16 §2.3.1. Allowable
   stress combinations (ASD) per §2.4 are used only for soil-structure interaction checks at the geotechnical
   interface (bearing pressure, settlement) and are stated in the geotechnical calculation package. Load combinations
   relevant to Package A are set out in full below.

   6.1 Basic Strength Load Combinations — ASCE 7-16 §2.3.1
           (1) 1.4D
           (2) 1.2D + 1.6L + 0.5(Lr or S or R)
           (3) 1.2D + 1.6(Lr or S or R) + (L or 0.5W)
           (4) 1.2D + 1.0W + L + 0.5(Lr or S or R)
           (5) 1.2D + Ev + Eh + L + 0.2S

   Where:

         0.2·SDS·D and horizontal Eh = ρ·QE component.

   6.2 Counteracting Combinations — ASCE 7-16 §2.3.1(6)–(7)

   compounds) the effect of the variable load. These combinations apply

   PART 1 — SCOPE
   1.1 General
   This document constitutes the dewatering and groundwater control plan required under Specification Section 31
   23 19 for construction of the Block A basement excavation on Package A of the Birchwood Village Expansion
   Program. It defines the design assumptions, method of dewatering, discharge arrangement, monitoring provisions
   and limitations of the temporary works.

   1.2 Scope of Work — Explicit
   This dewatering plan addresses dewatering of the Block A basement excavation only, to subgrade El. 730.0
   approximate. It does NOT extend to the separate deep excavation planned beneath Block B, which will be
   addressed by a separate delegated design.
   For the avoidance of doubt: no interior drawdown system is proposed for Block B under this plan; groundwater
   within the Block B enclosure will be managed by sump control of surface and construction water only. The Block
   B plant-room excavation is enclosed by a separate slurry cutoff wall keyed a minimum of 4 ft into the
   compressible clay stratum (toe at El. 722.0), covered under a separate submittal.
   The following are expressly outside the scope of this submittal:
     (a) Any excavation, cofferdam, cutoff wall or shoring system beneath, adjacent to, or in support of construction
         other than the Block A basement excavation defined above;
     (b) Any dewatering operation targeted at, or intended to relieve pressure in, the confined aquifer underlying the
         site (see Part 4 — Limitations);
     (c) Any groundwater control associated with the deeper subsurface work planned under Block B, which is being
         carried under a separate submittal package by others.
   Any subsequent excavation extending below approximate El. 730.0, or approaching the confined aquifer beneath
   the compressible clay aquitard, will require a separately-sealed dewatering and groundwater control analysis.
   Nothing in this submittal shall be relied upon to demonstrate stability of, or groundwater control for, work outside
   the Block A basement footprint defined in Article 1.1.

   1.3 Reference Documents
    • Geotechnical Investigation Report, Birchwood Village Package A, Kelbrook Geotechnical, Inc., Report No.
       KGI-2024-0417, Rev.2, 02/14/2025. (Referenced herein as "the Geotechnical Report.")

                                                              Page 3
     • Structural Sheet S-102, Package A, Calloway Braddock Structural Engineers, LLC (basement mat plan and
       elevations).
    • Specification Section 31 23 19 — Dewatering.

   2.1 Summary of Subsurface Profile

    Compressible Clay           El. 738.0 to El. 720.0       Normally-consolidated, medium      CL          Low
    Aquitard                                                 plasticity clay, 18 ft thick

   2.2 Groundwater Regime
   Groundwater conditions applicable to the Block A basement excavation are as described in Section 7 of the
   Geotechnical Report and are summarized below.
   Design water table (upper sand): El. 742.0 ft. Shallow standpipe monitoring across the site from 11/22/2024
   through the period preceding this submittal has produced readings between El. 741.6 and El. 742.4, and El. 742.0
   is adopted as the design water table for the upper phreatic surface. Seepage at El. 741.8 to El. 742.2 has been
   observed at the perimeter of preliminary test pits in the upper sand.
   Confined piezometric head (deep aquifer): El. 738.0 ft. Deep piezometers screened in the dense sand and
   gravel below El. 720.0 have produced readings between El. 737.7 and El. 738.3, confirming a confined
   piezometric head at El. 738.0. This head is developed in the confined sand and gravel aquifer below El. 720.0 and
   is hydraulically separated from the upper sand by the intervening clay aquitard (El. 738.0 down to El. 720.0).
   Aquitard. The 18-ft-thick clay stratum between El. 738.0 and El. 720.0 acts as an aquitard between the shallow
   phreatic surface in the upper sand and the confined aquifer below. Its low mass permeability is such that, for the
   durations and hydraulic gradients associated with construction dewatering of the upper sand, no meaningful
   vertical hydraulic communication is developed across it.
