   PART 3 — METHOD OF DEWATERING
   3.1 Selected Method
   Dewatering of the Block A basement excavation shall be accomplished by a single-stage perimeter well-point
   system installed in the upper sand around the Block A basement footprint. Well points shall draw the upper
   phreatic surface down from El. 742.0 to a working elevation of El. 728.0 (approximately 2 ft below the design
   subgrade of El. 730.0) for the duration of below-grade construction within Block A.
   The well-point system is intended solely to relieve the shallow phreatic surface in the upper sand within the Block
   A footprint. It is not designed to, and does not, address the confined piezometric head in the deep aquifer (see Part
   4).

   3.2 Well-Point Layout
   Twenty-four (24) well points shall be installed around the perimeter of the Block A basement excavation,
   arranged approximately as follows:

    Perimeter Segment                         Length (approx.)         Well-Point Spacing             No. of Well Points
    North perimeter (Line 1)                  90 ft                    15 ft o.c.                     6
    East perimeter (Line G)                   90 ft                    15 ft o.c.                     6
    South perimeter (Line 4)                  90 ft                    15 ft o.c.                     6
    West perimeter (Line A)                   90 ft                    15 ft o.c.                     6
    Total                                                                                             24

   Well-point details:
    • Riser: 2-inch nominal Schedule 40 PVC, jetted-in.
    • Screen: 2-inch nominal PVC screen, slot 0.020 in, 5 ft length, seated between approximately El. 738.5 and El.
       733.5.
    • Filter pack: uniform silica sand, 20/40, placed to at least 1 ft above screen.
    • Header main: 6-inch nominal HDPE header, welded joints, laid at approximately El. 745, connected to well
       points via flexible swing-arm risers.
    • Pumps: two (2) Thompson 6 in diesel wellpoint pumps, one duty and one standby, sized for the combined
       discharge with 25% reserve capacity; automatic transfer on primary loss of vacuum or flow.
    • Vacuum: system designed for steady-state vacuum of 20 to 25 in Hg at the header main.
   Each well-point riser shall be capped with a shut-off valve at the header connection to allow individual isolation
   for maintenance without shutdown of the surrounding system.

   3.3 Startup and Steady-State Operation



Submittal 31-DW-A Rev.1 — Dewatering and Groundwater Control Plan                             Birchwood Village Expansion — Package A
                                                              Page 5
    Startup shall commence not less than fourteen (14) calendar days prior to the beginning of below-grade
   excavation within Block A. Excavation shall not proceed until:
     (a) The observed drawdown at the interior of the Block A footprint has stabilized at or below El. 728.0 for not
         less than seventy-two (72) continuous hours, and
     (b) All three shallow observation piezometers (see Article 3.5) have produced readings within 0.3 ft of the
        target drawdown for two consecutive twice-daily reads.
   Steady-state pumping shall continue continuously (24 hours per day, 7 days per week) from startup through
   completion of the basement mat, exterior basement wall waterproofing, and backfill of the exterior wall to a level
   adequate to resist buoyancy of the mat under design head. Shutdown shall be executed by the Contractor only
   with written concurrence of the Owner's Representative.

   3.4 Discharge
   Discharge from the well-point pumps shall be routed to the campus storm sewer system, in accordance with the
   discharge permit obtained by the Contractor from the City of Columbus. Discharge routing is as follows:
    • Header main discharge → in-line flow meter and sediment trap → 8-inch HDPE lay-flat conveyance line →
       sediment control basin at Grid J-7 (approx. 40 ft × 20 ft × 4 ft deep, lined) → outfall pipe to existing storm
       manhole SM-14 at the northwest corner of the site.
   Design steady-state discharge is estimated at 55 gpm from the combined system (based on Sichardt-type radius of
   influence calculations for the upper sand with representative permeability of 5 × 10-3 cm/s). The discharge permit
   obtained by the Contractor is issued for peak flows up to 100 gpm.
   Water quality at the discharge point shall be checked twice weekly for turbidity and pH; results shall be recorded
   in the dewatering log required under Article 3.6.

   3.5 Monitoring — Shallow Piezometers
   Drawdown of the upper phreatic surface shall be monitored by three (3) shallow standpipe observation
   piezometers, installed within the Block A footprint prior to startup. Piezometer locations shall be selected to
   represent the interior response of the excavation:
    • OP-1: approximate center of Block A footprint.
    • OP-2: midway between the west perimeter well-point line and the geometric center.
    • OP-3: midway between the north perimeter well-point line and the geometric center.
   Each observation piezometer shall be a 2-inch PVC standpipe with a 5-ft screen set between approximately El.
   738 and El. 733, sanded around the screen and grouted above. Water levels shall be read twice daily during
   startup, once daily during steady-state operation, and hourly during any period when a duty pump is out of
   service.
   Readings shall be recorded in a dewatering log maintained by the Contractor's superintendent and made available
   to the Owner's Representative on request. The log shall record: date and time; pump status (duty/standby);
   observed water level at OP-1, OP-2, OP-3; system vacuum; header main discharge flow; discharge turbidity and
   pH (twice weekly); and any operational events (pump changeover, header repair, weather).

   3.6 Contingency
   Loss of drawdown at any of the three observation piezometers by more than 1.0 ft from the target El. 728.0,
   sustained for more than four (4) hours during active excavation or four (4) hours during any 24-hour period of
   steady-state operation, shall constitute a system exception. On any such exception the Contractor shall:
     (a) Immediately transfer to the standby pump and diagnose the duty pump;


Submittal 31-DW-A Rev.1 — Dewatering and Groundwater Control Plan                  Birchwood Village Expansion — Package A
                                                              Page 6
      (b) Notify the Owner's Representative and the Structural Engineer of Record in writing within four (4) hours;
         and
     (c) Suspend any excavation activity within Block A until the drawdown target is re-established.

   PART 4 — LIMITATIONS
   4.1 Confined Aquifer
   Because the confined aquifer at El. 720.0 is separated from the upper sand by the CL aquitard El. 738.0 to El.
   720.0, dewatering by perimeter well points in the upper sand will not reduce the confined head. The confined
   piezometric head at El. 738.0 is developed in the deep sand and gravel below El. 720.0 and is sustained by a
   source of recharge that is hydraulically decoupled from the shallow phreatic surface targeted by this system.
   Any excavation extending toward or into the confined aquifer will require separate analysis. Such analysis shall
   address, at minimum: (a) the residual thickness of the clay aquitard beneath the excavation subgrade; (b) the
   weight of that residual plug relative to the confined uplift acting on its underside at El. 720.0; (c) the factor of
   safety against base heave; and (d) whether relief of the confined head, by means outside the scope of this
   submittal (e.g., deep relief wells screened in the sand and gravel), is required to establish an adequate factor of
   safety.
   Nothing in this submittal has been designed to, and nothing in this submittal shall be construed to, relieve the
   confined piezometric head.

   4.2 Adjacent and Subsequent Work
   This plan is limited to the Block A basement excavation defined in Article 1.2. It shall not be relied upon by
   others as the basis for:
     (a) Design of temporary shoring outside the Block A footprint;
     (b) Design of excavation support, cofferdams or cutoff walls beneath Block B or elsewhere on the site;
     (c) Any calculation that treats the excavation as dry, dewatered or relieved outside the extents shown in Article
         3.2 above;
     (d) Any design that assumes a reduction in the confined piezometric head below El. 738.0 at any location.
   Any delegated design outside the Block A basement footprint shall independently verify the groundwater
   conditions applicable to that work directly from the Geotechnical Report or from a separately-sealed
   hydrogeologic evaluation. The undersigned engineer's seal below applies only to the temporary works described
   in this submittal, within the scope defined in Article 1.2, and only for the Block A basement excavation.

   4.3 Duration
   This plan is prepared for the temporary construction duration of the Block A below-grade work. It does not
   constitute a permanent groundwater control system and does not address long-term dewatering. Permanent
   below-grade water management for the completed structure is addressed under separate design by the Architect
   of Record and Structural Engineer of Record (below-grade waterproofing and drainage details, see Package A
   architectural and structural documents).

   4.4 Weather and Recharge
   The upper sand phreatic surface in the vicinity of the excavation may respond to seasonal recharge from
   significant precipitation events. The 25% reserve pump capacity provided under Article 3.2 is intended to
   accommodate ordinary seasonal fluctuation. Extraordinary precipitation events (e.g., a 10-year 24-hour event)
   may require additional temporary measures to be added by the Contractor.

PART 1    GENERAL
   1.1 SUMMARY
   A. Section Includes:
         1. Excavation, subgrade preparation, and grading for building foundations, mat foundations,
            pile caps, footings, and slabs-on-grade within the Package A limits of work.
         2.    Placement, moisture-conditioning, and compaction of engineered structural fill under
              building foundations and slabs-on-grade.
         3. Backfill against foundation walls and around subsurface structures.
         4. Field quality control by the Owner's independent testing laboratory.
   B. Related Sections:
         1.    Section 31 23 33 — Trenching and Backfilling for utility trenches within the building
              envelope.
         2. Section 31 50 00 — Excavation Support and Protection for delegated shoring design.
         3. Section 03 30 00 — Cast-in-Place Concrete for placement of concrete against completed
            subgrade.
   1.2 REFERENCES
   A.    Referenced Standards. The following standards are incorporated by reference to the extent
         cited herein. The latest edition in effect at the date of Contract award shall govern.
         1.   ASTM D698 — Standard Test Methods for Laboratory Compaction Characteristics of
              Soil Using Standard Effort (Standard Proctor). Cited for historical borrow characterization
              only; not the acceptance basis for Package A structural fill.
         2.   ASTM D1557 — Standard Test Methods for Laboratory Compaction Characteristics of
              Soil Using Modified Effort (Modified Proctor). Governing laboratory reference for
              Package A structural fill.
         3. ASTM D6938 — Standard Test Methods for In-Place Density and Water Content of Soil
            and Soil-Aggregate by Nuclear Methods (Shallow Depth). Governing field density test
            method.
         4.     ASTM D2216 — Standard Test Methods for Laboratory Determination of Water
              (Moisture) Content of Soil and Rock by Mass. Referee method for moisture content
                                         31 20 00 - Page 1 of 6

           when the nuclear gauge reading is disputed.
     5. ASTM D2937 — Standard Test Method for Density of Soil in Place by the Drive-Cylinder
        Method. Alternate field density method where permitted in writing by the Structural
        Engineer of Record.
1.3 DEFINITIONS
A.   Structural Fill: Imported or on-site engineered soil placed and compacted in controlled lifts
     beneath building foundations, mat foundations, pile caps, footings, or slabs-on-grade, and
     meeting the material, gradation, and compaction requirements of this Section.
B. Common Fill: Non-structural earth used only for site grading outside the building envelope.
C.    Lift: A single layer of loose fill placed in preparation for compaction, not exceeding the
     maximum loose lift thickness specified in Part 3.
D.    Test Location: A single field-density test point at which both dry density and moisture
     content are measured for compliance evaluation.
E.    Placed Material: The specific soil material actually placed in the field at the test location,
     whose laboratory maximum dry density and optimum moisture content have been established
     by ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory testing prior to placement, as required by Article 2.1.
1.4 QUALITY ASSURANCE
A. Testing Laboratory. Field and laboratory testing under this Section shall be performed by the
   Owner's independent construction materials testing laboratory (the “Laboratory”), contracted
   directly to the Owner. The Contractor shall coordinate access, sampling opportunity, and
   lift-by-lift notification with the Laboratory.
B.    Personnel. Nuclear-gauge operators shall hold current radiation safety training and shall be
     documented as competent in ASTM D6938 direct-transmission procedures. Nuclear gauges
     shall be calibrated within the manufacturer's stated interval and standard-count checked at
     the start of each testing day.
C.     Placed-Material Correspondence. The laboratory maximum dry density and optimum
     moisture content used as the acceptance denominators for any test location shall be those
     determined by ASTM D1557 Method C on the material actually placed at that location. Where
     the placed material differs materially from the previously characterized borrow, a new ASTM
     D1557 Method C test shall be performed on the new material before further fill placement is
     accepted.
1.5 SUBMITTALS
A. Prior to structural fill placement, submit for review:
     1.    Source identification for each proposed borrow, including gradation (sieve analysis),
          Atterberg limits, and USCS classification.
     2.   Laboratory report of maximum dry density and optimum moisture content per ASTM
          D1557 Method C for each proposed source material.
     3.    Placement and compaction plan identifying lift thickness, compaction equipment, and
          passes.
B. During placement, submit daily:
                                     31 20 00 - Page 2 of 6
                                         Earth Moving
          1. Field density reports per ASTM D6938 identifying test location, lift number, elevation, dry
            density, moisture content, the ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory maximum dry density
            and optimum moisture content used as denominators, percent compaction, and moisture
            deviation from optimum.
   1.6 SEQUENCING
   A.     No structural fill shall be placed until the underlying subgrade has been proof-rolled in the
         presence of the Laboratory and accepted in writing by the Owner's Representative Engineer.
   B.     No fill placement shall proceed on any lift until the preceding lift has been tested and
         accepted per Article 3.4.
PART 2    PRODUCTS
   2.1 STRUCTURAL FILL
   A.     Material. Well-graded granular fill classified SM or SW-SM, laboratory-tested per ASTM
         D1557 Method C (modified Proctor) prior to placement.
   B.     Gradation. Structural fill shall meet the following gradation, with no more than 12% passing
         the No. 200 sieve and a plasticity index not exceeding 6.
   C.     Deleterious Material. Structural fill shall be free of organic material, frozen soil, debris, and
         particles greater than 3 inches in largest dimension.
   D.    Laboratory Characterization. For each source and for each material change, the Laboratory
         shall determine the maximum dry density and optimum moisture content by ASTM D1557
         Method C prior to placement. The resulting laboratory values are the denominators against
         which the acceptance criteria of Article 3.4.B are evaluated.
   2.2 COMMON FILL
   A. Common fill placed outside the building envelope shall be free of organic material, debris, and
      frozen soil, but is not subject to the acceptance criteria of Article 3.4.B.
   2.3 CAPILLARY BREAK / DRAINAGE COURSE
   A. Clean, open-graded crushed stone, 3/4 in nominal, less than 2% passing the No. 200 sieve,
      placed as shown on the Drawings beneath slabs-on-grade.
PART 3    EXECUTION
   3.1 EXAMINATION
   A.     Examine subgrade prior to fill placement. Do not proceed with fill placement over subgrade
         that is soft, yielding under proof roll, frozen, or otherwise unsuitable. Notify the Owner's
         Representative Engineer in writing of any unsuitable subgrade condition.
   3.2 SUBGRADE PREPARATION
   A. Strip topsoil, organic material, and any existing uncontrolled fill from beneath the footprint of
      structural fill.
   B. Proof-roll exposed subgrade with a loaded tandem-axle dump truck or equivalent equipment
      approved in writing by the Owner's Representative Engineer. The Laboratory shall be present
                                          31 20 00 - Page 3 of 6
                                              Earth Moving
      to witness the proof roll.
C.    Undercut and replace yielding areas with structural fill placed and compacted per this
     Section.
3.3 PLACEMENT
A. Place structural fill in horizontal lifts not exceeding 12 inches loose thickness.
B.    Moisture-condition each lift, by wetting or drying and mixing, so that the moisture content at
     the time of compaction is within the range specified in Article 3.4.B.
C.    Compact each lift with equipment sized and operated to achieve the density and moisture
     requirements of Article 3.4.B throughout the full thickness of the lift.
D.     Do not place fill on frozen subgrade or with frozen material. Do not place fill during
     precipitation that raises the placed material's moisture content above the upper limit of Article
     3.4.B.
3.4 COMPACTION
A. Method Statement. The Contractor shall place structural fill in controlled lifts as specified in
   Article 3.3, moisture-conditioning each lift as necessary to bring the material within the
   moisture range required by Article 3.4.B before compaction. Compaction equipment
   (self-propelled vibratory smooth-drum rollers, pad-foot rollers, or plate compactors adjacent to
   structures) shall be operated in a pattern of overlapping passes such that every location
   within a lift receives no fewer than the number of passes established during a
   Contractor-conducted test strip witnessed by the Laboratory and the Owner's Representative
   Engineer. The test strip shall be executed at the start of production placement, using the
   placement source, moisture-conditioning method, lift thickness, and compaction equipment
   intended for production, and shall demonstrate that the criteria of Article 3.4.B are met before
   general production is authorized. Adjacent to walls, columns, and utilities, use hand-operated
   compaction equipment in lifts not exceeding 6 inches loose thickness. Do not operate heavy
   compaction equipment within 3 feet of walls prior to backfill balancing on both sides. Each lift
   shall be tested and accepted per Article 3.4.B before the next lift is placed.
B. Acceptance Criteria.
             Structural fill shall be placed and compacted to a dry density of not less than
             95% of the maximum dry density determined by ASTM D1557 Method C for the
             placed material, AND shall be placed at a moisture content within −1% to +2%
             of the optimum moisture content determined by the same test. Both criteria must
             be satisfied for each test location. Field density shall be measured per ASTM
             D6938 (nuclear gauge, direct-transmission mode) at a frequency of one test per
             5,000 sf per lift.
C.   Failing Tests. Where either the density criterion or the moisture criterion of Article 3.4.B is
     not satisfied at any test location:
     1.    The affected area of the lift shall be reworked (scarified, moisture-conditioned, and
          recompacted, or removed and replaced) at the Contractor's expense.
     2.    Reworked areas shall be retested by the Laboratory. Both the density and moisture
          criteria of Article 3.4.B must be satisfied on the retest before the lift is accepted.
                                     31 20 00 - Page 4 of 6
                                         Earth Moving
      3.   Isolated failing tests may not be averaged with adjacent passing tests to demonstrate
          compliance. Acceptance is evaluated at each test location independently.
D.    Interpretation. No test location shall be accepted on the basis of density alone. No test
     location shall be accepted on the basis of moisture alone. Compliance requires that both the
     density criterion and the moisture criterion of Article 3.4.B be independently satisfied at that
     test location, as measured against the ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory maximum dry
     density and optimum moisture content of the material actually placed at that location.
3.5 BACKFILL AGAINST FOUNDATION WALLS
A. Do not commence backfill against basement or foundation walls until the wall has attained its
   specified 28-day compressive strength, or until permanent lateral support (floor framing) is in
   place and grouted to the wall, whichever occurs first.
B.    Place backfill on both sides of interior walls in balanced lifts not exceeding 12 inches loose
     thickness, differing by no more than one lift side-to-side.
C. Compact backfill to the same acceptance criteria as Article 3.4.B where the backfill supports
   structure or slabs; elsewhere, to 90% of ASTM D1557 Method C maximum dry density.
3.6 SETTLEMENT TOLERANCE
A.   Total and Differential Settlement. Total settlement 1.0 in maximum; differential settlement
     0.5 in maximum over 30 ft.
B.    Application. The tolerances of Paragraph A apply to the completed foundation system as
     constructed on the accepted subgrade and structural fill delivered under this Section. Where
     predicted or monitored settlements exceed the tolerances of Paragraph A, the Structural
     Engineer of Record shall be notified in writing and no additional load shall be applied until a
     written disposition is issued.
C.    Monitoring. Where settlement monitoring points are shown on the Drawings, readings shall
     be taken and transmitted to the Owner's Representative Engineer at the frequency indicated.
     Cumulative settlement approaching either tolerance of Paragraph A shall be reported
     immediately.
3.7 FIELD QUALITY CONTROL
A. Testing frequency for structural fill:
     1. In-place density and moisture: one ASTM D6938 test per 5,000 sf per lift, as required by
        Article 3.4.B, and not fewer than three tests per lift regardless of lift area.
     2.    Laboratory maximum dry density and optimum moisture content: one ASTM D1557
          Method C determination per source, and one additional determination for each material
          change identified by visual classification or gradation.
B.    Reporting. The Laboratory shall issue field density reports within 24 hours of testing. Each
     report shall identify, for each test location, the ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory maximum
     dry density and optimum moisture content used as the denominators, the measured dry
     density, the measured moisture content, the percent compaction, the moisture deviation from
     optimum, and the disposition (accept or reject) against Article 3.4.B.
C.    Non-Conforming Work. Any lift not meeting Article 3.4.B, or any lift for which the ASTM
     D1557 Method C denominators used in reporting do not correspond to the material actually
     placed, shall be reworked as required by Article 3.4.C before any additional lift is placed.
                                      31 20 00 - Page 5 of 6
                                          Earth Moving
       3.8 PROTECTION
      A.     Protect accepted subgrade and completed structural fill from disturbance, softening by
           precipitation, freezing, and construction traffic until covered by permanent construction.

           permanent cover.

40 ["Samples tested comprise (a) recovered split-spoon (SPT) sub-samples from all nine borings for classification, moisture and grain-size analysis, and (b) thin-walled Shelby-tube (undisturbed) sub-specimens from the clay aquitard for unit-weight determination. EL_top, EL_sub, EL_wt, EL_clay_top, EL_aq = 750.0, 726.0, 742.0, 738.0, 720.0
g_fill, g_clay, g_sg = 118.0, 120.0, 130.0
Ka_f, Ka_c = 0.307, 0.390
q = 250.0
EL_anchor = 745.5

# ---------- R2.3 re-computation: layered effective stress active + hydrostatic ----------
def sigv_eff(el):
    # effective vertical stress behind wall incl. surcharge
    s = q
    # fill 750->738, WT at 742
    top = EL_top
    if el >= EL_wt:
        return s + g_fill*(top-el)
    s += g_fill*(top-EL_wt)
    if el >= EL_clay_top:
        return s + (g_fill-gw)*(EL_wt-el)
    s += (g_fill-gw)*(EL_wt-EL_clay_top)
    return s + (g_clay-gw)*(EL_clay_top-el)
def pa(el, layer):
    K = Ka_f if layer=='fill' else Ka_c
    return K*sigv_eff(el)
# integrate numerically
N=24000
F=0; M=0
for i in range(N):
    z0 = EL_top - i*(EL_top-EL_sub)/N
    z1 = EL_top - (i+1)*(EL_top-EL_sub)/N
    zm = 0.5*(z0+z1)
    layer = 'fill' if zm > EL_clay_top else 'clay'
    p = pa(zm, layer)
    dz = z0-z1
    F += p*dz
    M += p*dz*(EL_anchor-zm)
Pw = 0.5*gw*(EL_wt-EL_sub)**2
zw = EL_sub + (EL_wt-EL_sub)/3
Mw = Pw*(EL_anchor-zw)
print("R2.3 check:")

print(f"  Psoil = {F:.1f} lb/ft ; Msoil about 745.5 = {M:.0f} ; arm = {M/F:.3f}")
print(f"  Pw = {Pw:.1f} at El {zw:.2f}, arm {EL_anchor-zw:.3f}, Mw = {Mw:.0f}")
Ptot = F+Pw; MD = M+Mw

for su in (1400, 1100, 1000, 900):

        print(f"  su={su} D={D}: pn={pn:.0f} psf, Pp={Pp:.0f} lb/ft, arm={arm:.2f}, MR={MR:.0f}, FS={FS:.3f}")
# su required for FS 1.5 at D=6.5

print(f"  su required for FS=1.5 at D=6.5: {su_req:.0f} psf (Pp_req {Pp_req:.0f})")
print(f"  4su - sigma_v0 > 0 requires su > {sv0/4:.0f} psf")

print("\nDrained check below subgrade (Rev.1 §3.2 drained CL: phi'=26, c'=100, Kp=2.56, Ka=0.39):")
Kp, c = 2.56, 100.0
for case in ("hydrostatic","seepage_pumped"):

    layer = 'fill' if el > EL_clay_top else 'clay'

    sp.set(qn("w:before"), str(before)); sp.set(qn("w:after"), str(after))
    if line:
        sp.set(qn("w:line"), str(line)); sp.set(qn("w:lineRule"), "auto")
    ppr.append(sp)
    if ind_left is not None or hanging is not None:
        ind = OxmlElement("w:ind")
        if ind_left is not None: ind.set(qn("w:left"), str(ind_left))
        if hanging is not None: ind.set(qn("w:hanging"), str(hanging))
        ppr.append(ind)
    if align:
        jc = OxmlElement("w:jc"); jc.set(qn("w:val"), align); ppr.append(jc)
    p.append(ppr)
    if text:
        add_runs(p, text, size=size, bold=bold, italic=italic, color=color)
    return p

def para(text, **kw):
    kw.setdefault("line", 252)
    return make_p(text, **kw)

def subhead(text):
    return make_p(text, bold=True, before=160, after=60, keep_next=True)

def minor(text):
    return make_p(text, bold=True, before=80, after=40, keep_next=True, size=19)

def bullet(text, level=0):
    left = 360 + 300 * level
    return make_p(text, num=True, ind_left=left, hanging=220, after=50, line=252)

def lettered(label, text):
    return make_p(label + "\t" + text, ind_left=500, hanging=300, after=60, line=252)

def record(text):
    return make_p("Record: " + text, size=16, italic=True, color="595959", after=120, line=240)

def cell_props(tc, width, fill=None, valign="top"):
    tcpr = tc.find(qn("w:tcPr"))
    if tcpr is None:
        tcpr = OxmlElement("w:tcPr"); tc.insert(0, tcpr)
    w = OxmlElement("w:tcW"); w.set(qn("w:w"), str(width)); w.set(qn("w:type"), "dxa")
    tcpr.append(w)
    if fill:
        shd = OxmlElement("w:shd"); shd.set(qn("w:val"), "clear")
        shd.set(qn("w:color"), "auto"); shd.set(qn("w:fill"), fill)
        tcpr.append(shd)
    va = OxmlElement("w:vAlign"); va.set(qn("w:val"), valign); tcpr.append(va)

def make_table(widths, rows, header=True, size=17, shade_first_col=False, bold_first_col=False):
    """rows: list of lists of strings (markup allowed; '\n' splits paragraphs; lines
    starting with '• ' become indented bullet lines inside the cell)."""
    tbl = OxmlElement("w:tbl")
    tblpr = OxmlElement("w:tblPr")
    tw = OxmlElement("w:tblW"); tw.set(qn("w:w"), str(sum(widths))); tw.set(qn("w:type"), "dxa")
    tblpr.append(tw)
    borders = OxmlElement("w:tblBorders")
    for side in ("top", "left", "bottom", "right", "insideH", "insideV"):
        e = OxmlElement("w:" + side)
        e.set(qn("w:val"), "single"); e.set(qn("w:sz"), "4")
        e.set(qn("w:space"), "0"); e.set(qn("w:color"), "8C8C8C")
        borders.append(e)
    tblpr.append(borders)
    lay = OxmlElement("w:tblLayout"); lay.set(qn("w:type"), "fixed"); tblpr.append(lay)
    mar = OxmlElement("w:tblCellMar")
    for side, v in (("top", 30), ("left", 80), ("bottom", 30), ("right", 80)):
        e = OxmlElement("w:" + side); e.set(qn("w:w"), str(v)); e.set(qn("w:type"), "dxa")
        mar.append(e)
    tblpr.append(mar)
    tbl.append(tblpr)
    grid = OxmlElement("w:tblGrid")
    for w in widths:
        g = OxmlElement("w:gridCol"); g.set(qn("w:w"), str(w)); grid.append(g)
    tbl.append(grid)
    for ri, row in enumerate(rows):
        tr = OxmlElement("w:tr")
        trpr = OxmlElement("w:trPr")
        trpr.append(OxmlElement("w:cantSplit"))
        if header and ri == 0:
            trpr.append(OxmlElement("w:tblHeader"))
        tr.append(trpr)
        for ci, txt in enumerate(row):
            tc = OxmlElement("w:tc")
            is_head = header and ri == 0
            fill = "D9D9D9" if is_head else ("F2F2F2" if (shade_first_col and ci == 0) else None)
            cell_props(tc, widths[ci], fill=fill)
            lines = str(txt).split("\n")
            for li, line in enumerate(lines):
                if line.startswith("• "):
                    p = make_p("", after=20, ind_left=170, hanging=170, line=240)
                    add_runs(p, "•\t" + line[2:], size=size)
                else:
                    p = make_p("", after=20, line=240)
                    add_runs(p, line, size=size,
                             bold=(is_head or (bold_first_col and ci == 0)))
                tc.append(p)
            tr.append(tc)
        tbl.append(tr)
    return tbl

    return make_p("", after=after, size=8)

steps.message:
I've written and saved the verification memo, addressed to Rachel Marlbeck on the house form with its five sections and signature block kept. Its disposition is **NOT VERIFIED**: Item 048 stays **Open** and the 08/10/2026 excavation is not released.

**Why it doesn't verify** (all checked against the project record):
1. **Toe embedment.** Rev.2 uses an undrained shear strength (su) of 1,400 psf. The geotechnical report gives 900–1,100 psf, and the design basis memo says the report governs. On the logged values the factor of safety (FS) is 0.31–0.81 against 1.50 required. Kesterline's own check only passes if su is at least 1,378 psf. In the long-term drained condition the clay gives no net toe resistance at all.
2. **Tieback anchors.** At 20° with a 25 ft free and 24 ft bonded length, the bonded zone sits at El. 737.0–728.7, entirely in the clay. The 20 psi bond stress used is a sand-and-gravel value. Limited by the clay's strength, each anchor can carry at most 33.9–41.5 kips. The design load is 56.2 kips and the proof load 74.8 kips, so the anchors would fail proof testing.
3. **Base heave.** The arithmetic (FS 1.60) is right, but:
   - the stop-work trigger at El. 727.0 still lets FS drop to 1.48;
   - if pumping is lost at subgrade, FS is 0.58;
   - the relief-well system has no supporting design;
   - no Block B dewatering plan exists, and the Block A plan explicitly excludes Block B.
4. **Rev.2's supersession table points to the wrong Rev.1 sections.** As a result it leaves Rev.1's dry-excavation assumption and its El. 722.0 toe in force.
5. **Location.** Drawing S-101 Rev.4 puts the pit inside the completed basement mat (grids H–L / 3–5), with the southernmost row of piles on its north edge. Kesterline designed an open cut from El. 750.0 and states there are no structures nearby.

**Checks that can be carried forward as they stand:**
- the groundwater and soil-layer inputs, which match all 19 monitoring rounds and both borings inside the pit;
- the clay and gravel unit weights;
- the 250 psf construction surcharge;
- the PZ-35 sheet capacity;
- the wale capacity (up to 15,700 lb/ft).

Everything else cannot. That includes the Rev.2 load calculation: the arithmetic is right, but it takes the compacted fill at 118 pcf when the records show at least 132 pcf.

**Effect on the permanent work at Block B:**
- **Settlement and drag on the 48 piles and the mat.** Pumping the deep aquifer down 11.5 ft would compress the clay under the piles and mat. My estimate is about 0.8 in within 6 months, rising to about 2.4 in if sustained. That is the same order as the 1.0 in total / 0.5 in differential tolerance, and it adds drag load to the piles (the open Item 049 issue).
- **Ground movement and loss of support** at the north-edge piles and the mat beside the pit.
- **Anchors drilled into the pile group**, with no clash check.
- **Base blow-out and wall failure** if pumping fails.

**Required before excavation, and who produces it:**

| Deliverable | Produced by |
|---|---|
| Complete, consolidated sealed reissue of 31-SH-B | Kesterline, submitted through Rowan Bay |
| Separately sealed Block B dewatering plan | Rowan Bay |
| Assessment of effects on the permanent structure, plus clarification of the pit location | Calloway Braddock (Nash, EOR) |
| As-built survey and baseline monitoring | Rowan Bay |
| Confirmation of soil parameters | Kelbrook, on your instruction |

**08/10/2026:** not released, and not achievable. A complete package received on 07/27 would still have the 21-day review period running to 08/17, and the relief wells must then be installed and proven before excavation. The memo recommends asking for a revised schedule. It does not affect the 07/22 Level-3 pour.

**Register entry (memo §5.5):** NOT VERIFIED; response by A. Vance (Thelbridge); response date 07/20/2026; status Open; verification date "—".

Things you should know:
- **Register workbook:** I did not edit it; the entry is in the memo for you to record.
- **Pit location:** the conflict between S-101 and Kesterline's design is unresolved in the record. The memo asks the EOR to clarify rather than deciding it.
- **Settlement estimate:** this is indicative only, since nobody has yet modelled how far the pumping drawdown spreads.
- **Specifications not seen:** Sections 31 50 00 and 31 23 19 were not in the file; the conclusion doesn't depend on them.
- **Form changes:** I added a page-numbered footer, which the form does not have, and left the signature unsigned.
